span.p:
SC-002 alternate path, should
Given The same manager stopped mid-way through section 7 eight days ago. They remember almost nothing about where they were.

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: When They come back and say they want to carry on.

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see which sections are done, which are drafted, and which have not been started, with each grade

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They see that section 7 is at draft with two blocking defects, both named

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They are not asked any question they have already answered

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: They are asked the next question in section 7, in the vocabulary they established in ST-001

div.style: color: rgb(31, 36, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p: Then Work resumes at the first section that is not yet at review, no earlier answer is requested again, and the domain vocabulary is unchanged.
